answer:
I could only partly answer this. Three of the five numbers are confirmed, two are not, and only one mode is documented as returning without waiting.

**Numeric values**

| Mode | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Next | 0 | `NIIMAQdx.h` enum ([wpilibsuite/nivision](https://github.com/wpilibsuite/nivision/blob/master/cpp/include/Vision/NIIMAQdx.h)); pylablib gives the same, explicit `_int32(0)` ([pylablib NIIMAQdx_defs.py](https://github.com/AlexShkarin/pyLabLib/blob/main/pylablib/devices/IMAQdx/NIIMAQdx_defs.py)) |
| Last | 1 | same two sources |
| BufferNumber | 2 | same two sources |
| Every | **not found** | — |
| LastNew | **not found** | — |

Both headers I found list only Next, Last, BufferNumber and a Guard value (`0xFFFFFFFF`). Every and LastNew must be in a newer header or only in the LabVIEW enum. Web searches for `IMAQdxBufferNumberModeEvery` and `IMAQdxBufferNumberModeLastNew` returned nothing that defines them. You may have seen "Every = 3, LastNew = 4" somewhere; my sources neither confirm nor rule that out.

**Which mode returns without waiting**

- **Last:** NI's documentation says "the driver does not wait for the next buffer but instead returns the last acquired buffer." I read this wording in the search-result summaries ([documentation.help Get Image Data VI](https://documentation.help/NI-IMAQdx-VI/IMAQdx_Get_Image_Data.html)) and a quote in the [NI forum thread on Next vs. Every](https://forums.ni.com/t5/Machine-Vision/Buffer-Mode-quot-Next-quot-and-quot-Every-quot-in-IMAQdx-Extract/td-p/4079556). I couldn't open the page itself (HTTP 403).
- **Next:** waits for the next acquired buffer ([same](https://documentation.help/NI-IMAQdx-VI/IMAQdx_Get_Image_Data.html)).
- **BufferNumber:** "specifies an exact buffer number to wait for," so it blocks until that buffer exists (search-result summary of the same NI docs).
- **Every:** one forum post says it "returns all sequential images in memory," so buffers that are already queued come back quickly ([NI forum](https://forums.ni.com/t5/Machine-Vision/Buffer-Mode-quot-Next-quot-and-quot-Every-quot-in-IMAQdx-Extract/td-p/4079556); also [this thread](https://forums.ni.com/t5/Machine-Vision/Trying-to-understand-how-the-buffers-work-in-Imaqdx-aquisition/td-p/3986038)). That comes from forum users, not NI documentation. Nothing I found says what Every does when no un-read buffer is left, so I can't call it non-blocking.
- **LastNew:** NI has a knowledge-base article on exactly this, "[IMAQdx Get Image 2 VI: Buffer Number Mode 'Last' And 'Last New' Differences](https://knowledge.ni.com/KnowledgeArticleDetails?id=kA03q000001DwvoCAC&l=en-US)." Fetching it failed with a certificate error, so I can't say whether LastNew waits. The title suggests it differs from Last, but that's a guess.

**Bottom line:** Next = 0, Last = 1, BufferNumber = 2. The only mode documented as returning immediately is **Last**. For Every and LastNew, the numbers and blocking behaviour need NI's current documentation: the [IMAQdx Get Image2 VI page](https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-imaqdx-vi-ref/page/ni-imaqdx_vi_reference/imaqdx_get_image2.html), the KB article above, or the `NIIMAQdx.h` from your installed NI-IMAQdx. The ni.com docs pages loaded only as navigation, with no content, when I tried them.

Other sources checked: [pylablib IMAQdx module](https://pylablib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/pylablib/devices/IMAQdx/IMAQdx.html) (only uses the BufferNumber mode) and the [NI-IMAQdx C API page for IMAQdxGetImageData](https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/ni-imaqdx-c-api-ref/page/ni-imaqdx_function_reference/imaqdxgetimagedata.html) (loaded no content).
